slos.text: Explain, with examples, that civilizations throughout history have systematically studied living things [e.g., the history of numbers from Sumerians and its development to the present Arabic system.
Describe the set of real numbers as a combination of rational and irrational numbers.
Demonstrate and verify the properties of equality and inequality of real numbers.
Apply laws of indices to simplify radical expressions.
Express a number in scientific notations and vice versa.
Describe logarithm of a number.
Differentiate between common and natural logarithm.
Apply laws of logarithm to real life situations such as growth and decay, loudness of sound.
Apply concepts of rational numbers to real word problems (such as inventory (stock taking), temperature, banking, measures of gain and loss, sources of income and expenditure).
Describe mathematics as the Functions study of pattern, structure, and relationships.
Identify sets and apply operations on three sets (Subsets, overlapping sets and disjoint sets), using Venn diagrams
Solve problems on classification and cataloguing by using Venn diagrams for Scenarios involving two sets and three sets. Further
Verify and apply properties/laws of union and intersection of three sets through analytical and Venn diagram method.
Apply concepts from set theory to real world problems (such as in demographic classification, categorizing products in shopping malls and music playlist by genre) Relation.
Explain product, Binary Relations K and its domain and range.
Recognize that a relation can be represented by table, order pair and graphs.
Identify common factors, trinomial factoring, concretely, pictorially and symbolically.

Factorize quadratic and cubic algebraic expressions.  𝑎4 + 𝑎2 𝑏 2 + 𝑏 4 or 𝑎4 + 𝑏 4  𝑥 2 + 𝑝𝑥 + 𝑞  𝑎𝑥 2 + 𝑏𝑥 + 𝑐  (𝑎𝑥 2 + 𝑏𝑥 + 𝑐)(𝑎𝑥 2 + 𝑏𝑥 + 𝑑) + 𝑘  (𝑥 + 𝑎)(𝑥 + 𝑏)(𝑥 + 𝑐) + 𝑘  (𝑥 + 𝑎)(𝑥 + 𝑏)(𝑥 + 𝑐)(𝑥 + 𝑑) + 𝑘𝑥 2  𝑎3 + 3𝑎2 𝑏 + 3𝑎𝑏 2 + 𝑏 3  𝑎3 − 3𝑎2 𝑏 + 3𝑎𝑏 2 − 𝑏 3  𝑎3 ± 𝑏 3
Find highest common factor and least common multiple of algebraic expressions and know relationship of LCM and HCF.
Find square root of algebraic U/K expression by factorization and division.
Apply the concepts of factorization of quadratic and cubic algebraic A expressions to real world problems (such as engineering, physics, and finance.) Linear
Solve linear equations and Inequalities in one variable
Derive distance formula by Geometry locating the position of two points in coordinate plane
Calculate the midpoint of a line segment
Find the gradient of a straight line when coordinates of two points are given.
Find the equation of a straight K line in the form 𝒚 = 𝒎𝒙 + 𝒄
Find the gradient of parallel and U perpendicular lines.
Apply distance and midpoint formulas to solve real life situations such as physical measurements or distances between locations.
Apply concepts from coordinate Geometry to real world problems (such as, aviation and A navigation, landscaping, map reading, longitude and latitude).
Derive equation of a straight line in slope-intercept form, point-slope form, two-point form, intercepts form, symmetric form, normal form.
Show that a linear equation in two variables represents a straight line and reduce the U general form of the equation of a straight line to the other standard forms.
Find the angle between two Lines coplanar intersecting straight lines.
Find the equation of the family of lines passing through the point of intersection of two given lines.
Calculate angles of the triangle when the slopes of the sides are given. Logic
Differentiate between a mathematical statement and its proof.
Differentiate between an axiom, conjecture and theorem.
Formulate simple deductive proofs [algebraic proofs that require showing the LHS to be equal to the RHS. E.g., showing (𝒙 − 𝟑)𝟐 + 𝟓 = 𝒙𝟐 — 𝟔𝒙
Identify similarity of polygons. Area and Volume of Similar Figures
Solve problems using the relationship between areas of similar figures and volume of different solids
Solve real life problems that Properties of regular Polygons, Triangles and Parallelograms

Solve real life problems using the following loci and the method of intersecting loci for sets of points in two dimensions which are: at a given distance from a given point, at a given distance from a given straight line, equidistant from two given points equidistant from two given intersecting straight lines. Trigonometry
Identify angles in standard position, expressed in degrees and radians.
Apply Pythagoras’ theorem and the sine, cosine and tangent ratios for acute angles to find a side or of an angle of a right-angled triangle.
Solve real life trigonometric problems in two dimensions involving angles of elevation and depression.
Prove the trigonometric identities Identities relations.
Solve real life problems involving trigonometric identities.
Interpret and use three figure bearings.
Solve problems involving bearing.
Apply the concepts of trigonometry Construction of
Construct a triangle having given two sides and the included angle.
Construct a triangle having given one side and two of the angles.
Construct a triangle having given two of its sides and the angle opposite to one of them (with all the three possibilities).
Draw angle bisectors, perpendicular bisectors, medians, altitudes of a given triangle and verify their concurrency. Frequency
Construct a grouped frequency Distribution table, histogram (with unequal class intervals) and frequency polygon. Measure of
Calculate the mean modal class Tendency

Solve real life situations involving mean, weighted mean, median, and mode for given data (such as allocation of funds in different projects, forecasting future demographics, marketing, forecasting government budgets).
Calculate the probability of a single event and the probability of event not occurring
Solve real life problems involving probability
Calculate relative frequency as an estimate of probability.
Calculate expected frequencies. expected

Solve real life problems involving relative and expected frequencies.
